fact: PreGra's limited terms cover fading over 15% and UV pile-height loss over 50%, prorated over 0 to 4 years for a self-installed lawn and 0 to 10 years with PreGra Certified Installation, and cover the turf only, not installation or labor.
quote: PreGra also warrants that the Premium Artificial Grass product’s fiber will not color fade more than 15% from the original color. … PreGra also guarantees the pile height of the Premium Artificial Grass Product if it decreases by more than 50% of the original height due to ultraviolet radiation degradation. In such circumstances, PreGra will replace the affected portion of the finished Artificial Grass Product with a new Artificial Grass Product of equal quality based upon a prorated basis of 0 to 4 years with self-installation or 0 to 10 years with PreGra Certified Installation. This is for the turf only, excluding any incurred costs associated with the installation, including but not limited to labor charges, installation supplies, inconvenience, etc. … This warranty does not cover installation.
source_label: PreGra, 10-Year Manufacturer's Warranty terms (Warranty page)
notes: Proration chart on the same page: 0 through 4 years 100%, 5th year 70%, 6th 50%, 7th 30%, 8th and 9th 25%, 10th 20%. The page does not say how the chart applies to a self-installed lawn beyond the 0 to 4 year basis.

fact: PreGra's terms exclude failures from window-reflection heat, improper installation and low infill, and do not cover glue-down installs.
quote: Failures resulting from causes other than ultraviolet degradation of the face fiber yarn, such as excessive heat (heat from sun magnification from window reflection), improper installation, removal or reduction of the infill system level, chemical attack from adhesives, backing materials, cleaning agents, or any related causes are not covered by this warranty. This warranty does not protect glue-down applications.
source_label: PreGra, 10-Year Manufacturer's Warranty terms (Warranty page)

fact: PreGra's terms give a buyer 3 to 5 business days after delivery to report defects in writing, treat an unreported roll as accepted as is, and void coverage not registered within 30 days of purchase.
quote: Within 3 to 5 business days of delivery acceptance, the purchaser must inspect and notify PreGra, in writing, of any defects, shortages, or nonconformities. If the purchaser fails to notify PreGra of the defect, shortage, or nonconformity, PreGra will assume that the purchaser has accepted the product “as is.” … The warranty must be filled out, signed, and returned to PreGra within 30 days of purchase, or the warranty is voided.
source_label: PreGra, 10-Year Manufacturer's Warranty terms (Warranty page)

fact: SYNLawn's residential terms for its Lowe's channel, effective January 1, 2024, cover UV degradation, backing, yarns and tuft bind, prorated from 100% in years 1–3 to 15% in years 8–10.
quote: Specifically covered within the scope of this warranty: UV degradation, backing integrity, yarns and tuftbind. … Year 1 - 3 100% Year 4 - 5 50% Year 6 - 7 25% Year 8 - 10 15%
source_label: SYNLawn, Residential Statement of Warranty Terms and Conditions (Lowe's channel), effective January 1, 2024

fact: SYNLawn's Lowe's-channel terms say the turf must be installed by SYNLawn's own installers or to its installation guidelines, and also that properties installing the product themselves nullify the coverage.
quote: 3.2 Product must be installed by a SYNLawn® certified installer or in accordance with SYNLawn® Installation Guidelines. … 3.4 Product must be the recommended product for the installation as set forth in the SYNLawn® product guidelines and by certified SYNLawn installers; properties opting to install product themselves will nullify this warranty.
source_label: SYNLawn, Residential Statement of Warranty Terms and Conditions (Lowe's channel), effective January 1, 2024, sections 3.2 and 3.4
notes: The two sections pull against each other (3.2 allows installation to the guidelines; 3.4 says self-installation nullifies). Pages say so and tell the buyer to get the seller's answer in writing.

fact: SYNLawn's Lowe's-channel terms leave workmanship coverage to the installer, recommending 3 years, exclude acts of God and failures from improper subsurface preparation or drainage, and cover the product only, not the labor to fix a defect.
quote: Workmanship warranties remain the sole discretion between end user and installer; we recommend 3 years as this will ensure optimal project success. … Damages caused by vehicular traffic, vandalism, abuse, negligence or neglect, normal wear and tear and Acts of God. … Failure as a result of improper subsurface preparation or drainage. … Manufacturer is responsible for product only, not the installation labor required in conjunction with turf to remedy defect.
source_label: SYNLawn, Residential Statement of Warranty Terms and Conditions (Lowe's channel), effective January 1, 2024

fact: SYNLawn's Lowe's-channel terms ask for the paperwork within 45 days of purchase and route claims, due within 30 days of finding a defect, through the SYNLawn installer the turf was bought from.
quote: All documentation should be completed within 45 days of purchase including copy of paid invoice to installer. … Claims under this Warranty should be submitted to the certified SYNLawn® installer that the Product was purchased from. Claim must be submitted within thirty (30) days of discovery of the defect and within the warranty period.
source_label: SYNLawn, Residential Statement of Warranty Terms and Conditions (Lowe's channel), effective January 1, 2024

fact: SYNLawn's DIY installation guidelines, posted as a Lowe's product document, say the turf is sold in 15-foot widths by the linear foot, that a 7-foot-wide area still takes a 15-foot-wide piece, and that non-professional installs can leave seams more visible.
quote: The turf is sold in 15’ widths by whatever linear feet you order (example 15’ x 20’). … Note for Area 2: Even though this area is only 7’ wide, you must purchase in 15’ widths. So you would need a 15’ x 9’ piece of turf for this area and would have an 8’ x 9’ piece of turf leftover. … Note: The seaming process can be tricky. Professional installers are trained to hide seams so they are almost invisible. Please be aware that non-professional installations could result in more visibility to the seams.
source_label: SYNLawn, DIY Installation Guidelines for SYNLawn Artificial Grass (Lowe's product document)

fact: SYNLawn's DIY guidelines estimate seam adhesive in quarts of Henry's glue or tubes of Heavy Duty Liquid Nails.
quote: Adhesive: 1 qt. of Henry’s glue will cover about 15-20’ or one tube of Heavy Duty Liquid Nails covers about 20 linear ft.
source_label: SYNLawn, DIY Installation Guidelines for SYNLawn Artificial Grass (Lowe's product document)

fact: A February 2021 distributor spec book for Home Depot's TrafficMaster turf lists TrafficMaster 72 at 71.58 oz/yd² total weight and 42.78 oz/yd² of pile yarn, TrafficMaster 94 at 87.92 and 67.00, and TrafficMaster 108 at 109.22 and 79.84, with tuft binds of 15.9, 10.4 and 11.5 lbs.
quote: Turf Distributors Product Name The Home Depot Product Name … Eco 72 Silver TrafficMaster 72 … Eco 94 Gold TrafficMaster 94 Eco 108 Gold TrafficMaster 108 … TrafficMaster | 72 … Approximate Pile Height 1.5 in. … Total Product Weight 71.58 oz/yd² Pile Yarn Weight 42.78 oz/yd² Average Tuft Bind Strength 15.9 lbs/force … TrafficMaster | 94 … Approximate Pile Height 2.0 in. … Total Product Weight 87.92 oz/yd² Pile Yarn Weight 67.00 oz/yd² Average Tuft Bind Strength 10.4 lbs/force … TrafficMaster | 108 … Approximate Pile Height 1.77 in. … Total Product Weight 109.22 oz/yd² Pile Yarn Weight 79.84 oz/yd² Average Tuft Bind Strength 11.5 lbs/force

Current Home Depot listings could not be read (homedepot.com returns 403 to automated fetches), so pages date these figures to 2021 and tell buyers to ask for the current sheet.

fact: The same 2021 book's TrafficMaster terms pair an 8-year manufacturer term with a seller's residual term, prorated, that starts in year 9 and runs to 16 years, cover the material only, not installation workmanship, exclude the labor to remove and replace turf, and require claims within 30 days of discovering a defect.
quote: The above model sold and installed in USA is an 8 year warranty by Seller. … an additional eight (8) year period by Seller in addition to the manufacturer’s warranty of eight (8) years, for a total combined manufacturer and Seller Warranty period of sixteen (16) years from the date of shipment of Material to the Original Purchaser. … will only become effective on the first (1st) day of the ninth (9th) year after the date of shipment of Material to the Original Purchaser. … This Warranty is to be prorated as follows: … This Warranty applies only to the Material and Seller does not warrant against workmanship of the installation of the Material or any products used in the installation of the Material. … In no event will Seller be liable for any consequential, special, indirect, incidental or expectation damages, including, but not limited to, lost profits, lost revenue, loss of use, the labor cost of removal, the labor cost of replacement of the Material, or freight. … Claims must be submitted within 30 days after discovery of the alleged defects.
source_label: Turf Distributors, Artificial Turf Guide for The Home Depot's TrafficMaster turf (PDF created February 2021), 16 Year Warranty pages
notes: The 16-year residual term is prorated 100% in years 9 to 11, 50% in years 12 to 14 and 25% in years 15 to 16. Delivery defects in writing within 60 days of arrival. TrafficMaster 48 carried a 4-year term instead.

fact: The Synthetic Turf Council defines face weight as the total weight of the yarn above the backing and says most landscape grass falls between 40 and 100 oz per square yard.
quote: Total Yarn Weight (aka Face Weight) Total weight of the yarn above the backing. … Most synthetic grass has a pile height of between 1½” and 2”, and a density of between ¼” and ½” for a total yarn weight of between 40 oz. and 100 oz. per square yard.
source_label: Synthetic Turf Council, Considerations When Buying Synthetic Grass for Landscape Use (September 2013), Quality Guidelines

fact: The Synthetic Turf Council's landscape buying guidelines recommend a dual primary backing of at least 7 oz per square yard, a tuft bind of 6.8 lbs or more, and yarn UV results from an independent lab after 3000 hours of UVA testing.
quote: The STC recommends a system with a dual primary backing with a weight of at least 7 oz. per square yard. … The STC recommends a tuft bind of 6.8 lbs., but the higher the tuft bind, the better. … Yarn Characteristics (Should be validated in report by an Independent Test Lab) … UV resistance of fibers … 3000 hrs. UVA testing
source_label: Synthetic Turf Council, Considerations When Buying Synthetic Grass for Landscape Use (September 2013), Quality Guidelines

fact: The Synthetic Turf Council tells buyers to confirm seams will be bonded with an industrial synthetic-grass adhesive with proven weather resistance, which it says is usually not found in home supply stores.
quote: Confirmation that an industrial adhesive formulated for synthetic grass installations and with proven weather resistance, a product usually not found in home supply stores, will be used to bond the synthetic grass seams.
source_label: Synthetic Turf Council, Considerations When Buying Synthetic Grass for Landscape Use (September 2013), Guidelines for Prequalifying and Selecting a Professional Contractor

fact: The Synthetic Turf Council tells buyers to keep the sample they chose and compare it with the delivered turf, and to check that the roll's shipping label shows the same country of origin as the sample.
quote: Keep the synthetic grass sample you select, and compare it before installation to the product that is delivered. … The turf sample should identify where the turf was manufactured, e.g., USA or China. When the turf rolls are received, make sure to check the shipping label on the turf rolls and bill of lading to verify that the country of origin is the same as was originally represented;
source_label: Synthetic Turf Council, Considerations When Buying Synthetic Grass for Landscape Use (September 2013)

fact: EPA says UV intensity increases about 6% per kilometer of elevation above sea level.
quote: UV intensity increases about 6% per kilometer elevation above sea level.
source_label: U.S. EPA, Learn About the UV Index (Calculating the UV Index)
